title: Paperclip scientists in New Mexico mail Soviet-held colleagues
summary: Peter Levenda tells of Paperclip scientists in New Mexico mail Soviet-held colleagues, about late 1940s at New Mexico (no place named), and summarises it without a named source. As told, not a fact.

tellings.quote: >> Because the the the Russian scientists they had in New Mexico, >> right, were going into the village into the local towns and they were sending mail >> back to Germany which would then get sent over by Courier to the Russian scientists in the Soviet Union.

plain: Peter Levenda, an author who writes about secret history, tells a podcast host, Jesse Michels, about Operation Paperclip, the US programme that brought German scientists to America after the Second World War. He says that in the late 1940s scientists living in New Mexico would go into the local towns and mail letters back to Germany, and a courier then carried those letters to colleagues being held in the Soviet Union. If true, it would mean secrets were quietly passing between the two rival powers.
